title: Jimoke EVO-X5 Pro Mini PC Launched, Supports Local Smooth Operation of 300B Large Model with 192GB Memory

content_html:
At the just-opened IFA 2026 exhibition, the renowned hardware brand E-MoKe officially launched its highly anticipated new flagship mini PC - EVO-X5Pro. With top-tier hardware specifications and innovative architecture design, this product not only breaks through the ceiling of computing power in traditional small PCs, but also achieves a breakthrough capability to smoothly run a 300B parameter-level large language model on local devices.

Regarding the core processor and computing power configuration, the EVO-X5Pro is equipped with the AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO495 processor. This chip uses an advanced Zen5 architecture, featuring a powerful 16-core 32-thread specification with a maximum boost frequency of up to 5.2GHz. It also integrates a Radeon 8065S integrated graphics card based on the RDNA3.5 architecture, with 40 computing units, and a standalone NPU based on the XDNA2 architecture, providing 55TOPS of computing power, making the total computing power of the entire machine as high as an astonishing 131TOPS.

The memory subsystem is one of the most notable technical highlights of this machine. The device is equipped with up to 192GB of LPDDR5X-8533 unified memory with a bandwidth of up to 273GB/s. Among them, the maximum capacity of 160GB can be dynamically allocated as VRAM for direct GPU access. Since the CPU and integrated graphics share the same physical memory, it completely eliminates the data transfer overhead in traditional architectures. In actual testing, E-MoKe demonstrated using the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model at the exhibition site, achieving an output token speed of tens per second, maintaining a basically smooth interactive experience.

To handle the powerful hardware performance, E-MoKe has equipped the EVO-X5Pro with a VC heat plate and a three-fan intelligent cooling system, ensuring stable output under high load. The front panel of the machine has an F-MODE physical button that supports one-touch switching between three TDP presets. In terms of expansion and interface, the machine also performs comprehensively. The front panel provides 2 USB4 interfaces, while the back panel is equipped with 2 USB4V2 interfaces, supporting external graphics card docks and connecting multiple machines to form a distributed cluster; in addition, the machine is equipped with dual 10Gbps network ports (one with a speed of 10Gbps), fully meeting the needs of high-speed network transmission.

Currently, E-MoKe has only planned a 192GB top configuration version for this model, which is expected to be officially released in October 2026. The official has not yet announced the specific price. For users who do not have high memory demands in daily use, the company also stated that they can continue to choose the currently available previous generation Strix Halo series models.
